test_title: PYST 7: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.
 The scientist said that the results had been surprising.

options.text: The scientist said, "The results have been surprising."
The scientist said, "The results had been surprising."
The scientist said, "The results are surprising."
The scientist said, "The results were surprising."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• **Indirect Speech:** The scientist said that the results had been surprising. 
• **Key Conversions:** 
• **"have been surprising" becomes "had been surprising"** 
• Present perfect tense in direct speech changes to past perfect tense in indirect speech. 
• The verb backshifts from "have been" to "had been". 
• **Reporting verb:** 
• Indirect: "said that" 
• Converted to: "said," followed by quotation marks. 
• **Punctuation and Format:** 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks. 
• The reporting clause precedes the quoted speech, separated by a comma. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. **Correct Sentence:** *"The scientist said, "The results have been surprising.""* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1:** "The scientist said, "The results have been surprising."" 
• Correct because "have been" (present perfect) backshifts to "had been" (past perfect) in indirect speech. 
• **Option 2:** "The scientist said, "The results had been surprising."" 
• Incorrect because the direct sentence should typically be in a non-perfected past or present form. 
• **Option 3:** "The scientist said, "The results are surprising."" 
• Incorrect because present simple "are" changes to past simple "were". 
• **Option 4:** "The scientist said, "The results were surprising."" 
• While simple past can change to past perfect, the standard conversion for "had been" in this context is the present perfect "have been".
